title: Majestic Air!
summary: Place the bishop where it supports the checking route after both sides promote.

nodes.question: Where should the bishop clear the promotion square?
nodes.explanation: Ba8 blocks its own a7 pawn. Moving the bishop also changes whether Black can interpose a new queen against the later checking sequence.

branches.title: Sacrifice the bishop and win the queen
commentary: Begin after ...c3 in the complete six-piece study position. The promotional advertisement inserted in the source is outside this lesson.
Bg2 clears a8 while offering the bishop to Kg3. Crucially, the bishop now supports f3 on the later checking route.
c2 races the pawn instead of accepting the bishop.
a8=Q promotes, leaving the bishop on g2 to support the coming queen checks.
c1=Q gives Black a queen as well. Material is level, but the king placement and bishop support decide the tactics.
Qf3+ checks Kg3 horizontally, supported by Bg2. White starts the checking route toward the queen on c1.
Kh4 is the source’s illustrated king escape.
Qh3+ continues the king chase. This connecting check is independently supplied as a representative legal completion between the source’s saved Qf3 and Qh6 diagrams.
Kg5 is the illustrated king square in the final saved diagram, reached here through the independently supplied checking route.
Qh6+ skewers Kg5 and Qc1 along h6–g5–f4–e3–d2–c1.
Kf5 is an independently selected legal king retreat. It leaves the queen behind the king on that diagonal.
Qxc1 collects the queen. White has a checked winning queen-and-bishop ending; this is not an immediate mate.

branches.title: Accept the offered bishop
commentary: Compare the source’s alternative of taking the bishop on g2.
Bg2 offers the bishop while clearing the promotion square.
Kxg2 accepts, but steps onto the new queen’s promotion diagonal.
a8=Q+ promotes with check along a8–b7–c6–d5–e4–f3–g2. White gains the tempo needed to handle Black’s c-pawn; the exact position is a White win.
branches.explanation: a8=Q+ promotes with check along a8–b7–c6–d5–e4–f3–g2. White gains the tempo needed to handle Black’s c-pawn; the exact position is a White win.

branches.title: Clear the pawn with Bd5 instead
commentary: Compare the source’s initial failed attempt, with the bishop on d5 rather than g2.
Bd5 clears a8 but gives away the win. The bishop does not support the same checking route.
c2 continues Black’s promotion race.
a8=Q promotes first but does not check Kg3.
c1=Q restores the material balance and supplies defensive interpositions.
Qb8+ checks along b8–c7–d6–e5–f4–g3.
Qf4 interposes the new queen on that diagonal. The exact position is drawn: checking alone does not force the skewer found after Bg2.

exercises.prompt: Why does the bishop’s destination matter if either move clears a8?
exercises.answer: Bg2 supports f3, so the queen can approach the king along a useful checking route. Bd5 permits the defensive ...Qf4 interposition after Qb8+.

exercises.prompt: Why can White offer the bishop to the king?
exercises.answer: Kxg2 places the king on a8’s promotion diagonal, allowing a8=Q with check. That tempo keeps the race winning for White.
